why: Maximise a length: a longer piece never yields more pieces, so 'do the ribbons give at least k pieces of length L?' is true then false, and the answer is the last true L.
hints: How many pieces of length L does one ribbon of length r give? And all of them?
pieces(L) = sum(r // L) only goes down as L grows. Binary search the largest L in [1, max(ribbons)] with pieces(L) >= k.
Upper mid for 'last true'. O(n log max). Follow-up: with fractional lengths, loop a fixed number of times on real bounds instead of until lo == hi.
pitfalls: L = 0 would divide by zero: start the search at 1 (guaranteed feasible).
Pieces from different ribbons cannot be joined, so it is r // L per ribbon, not sum(r) // L.
